move: two squares slide in from opposite sides, VS pops, vote bars fill
how: A two-line title rises masked (yPercent 110→0, expo.out, stagger 0.1). Two square images slide in from x ∓700 with ∓8 rotation (move 0.8s) and meet at the centre while their inner layers settle from scale 1.2; a round VS badge spins in from scale 0 / rotation -120 with back.out(2.5), corner labels drop in, a 'Tap to vote' line and two result bars rise (power3.out, stagger 0.1). At 42% the vote lands: bar fills scaleX 0→0.62 and 0→0.38 (expo.out 1s) while a tweened object writes the percentages, the winning square lifts y -20 / scale 1.04 with back.out(2) and the loser shrinks to 0.96 with filter brightness 0.6; both inner images drift to scale 1.06. Exit at 84%: squares slide back out the way they came with expo.in, VS shrinks with back.in(2), title lines exit upward, bars and subline fade down.
adapt: Replace the two images and A/B labels, the title, bar names and the 62/38 split (both bars and the counter targets); keep the 0.8s opposing slide and the 1s expo.out fill at 1.7s.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the title, pair, VS, subline and bars; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with slide at 0.04D, vote at 0.42D, exit at 0.84D. The percentage object and its onUpdate must target el-scoped spans; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: backdrop-filter: blur(8px) on the corner labels
filter: brightness tween on the losing square
